claim: Close birds link only when their headings differ by less than 45°: 44° joins a group of three into a group of four, 46° leaves three strays and a fourth.
derivation: Two rows 16 apart on a 32 × 32 world. Row P: (4, 4), (5, 4), (6, 4) heading (1, 0), and P4 at (7, 4) heading 44°, v = (cos 44°, sin 44°). Row Q: (4, 20), (5, 20), (6, 20) heading (1, 0), and Q4 at (7, 20) heading 46°, v = (cos 46°, sin 46°).
Within a row, neighbours are 1 to 3 apart, below 4.5. Between rows the gap is 16, so no bird links across (E14).
P4's heading is 44° from P1–P3: cos 44° = 0.719340 > cos 45° = 0.707107, so it links, and P is one cluster of 4: one group.
Q4's heading is 46° from Q1–Q3: cos 46° = 0.694658 < cos 45°, so it does not link. Q1–Q3 are a cluster of 3 and Q4 a cluster of 1: strays. clusterCount = 1.
Unit headings: six (1, 0), one at 44° and one at 46°. Their sum is (7.413998, 1.413998), so directionalAgreement = 0.943454 (E12).
Every bird's nearest neighbour is 1 away, so meanNeighbourDistance = 1 (E13).
Strays: Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q4, 4 of 8 birds, so strayShare = 0.5 (E18). One group holding exactly half the birds: it reads as one group, since at least half is enough (O1).
The group is the row y = 4 (x = 4 to 7); its centre is (5.5, 4). Offsets ±0.5, ±1.5, so groupSpread = √1.25 (E19). No obstacles: birdsAtObstacles = 0 (E20).
